rounds.text: Modison Ltd is fundamentally under-appreciated, backed by a rules-based screen scoring an elite 97 out of 100 with high confidence [E63]. The company is executing exceptionally well, delivering explosive growth evidenced by a 67% compounded sales increase over the trailing twelve months [E17] and a massive 295% compounded profit growth over the same period [E21]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis puts intrinsic value at Rs 1281 per share against a market price of Rs 495, offering a substantial margin of safety of 61.4% [E45, E46]. Return metrics heavily support this valuation disconnect, with return on capital employed at 23.52% compared to a sector benchmark of 12.89% [E10], and an ROE of 26.41% against a sector benchmark of 10.82% [E9]. Management actively guides for this momentum to continue into the foreseeable future, driven by robust domestic and global demand for high and low voltage products [E74, E77]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -64 Cr in March 2026, alongside short-term borrowings rising to Rs 174 Cr [E34, E39].

A severe disconnect exists between Modison Ltd's reported earnings growth and its actual cash generation, highlighted by an alarming negative cash conversion of -0.88x for March 2026 [E33]. Operating cash flow plunged to negative Rs 64 Crore and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 79 Crore in March 2026, meaning operating cash flow represented only -36% of operating profit [E34, E35, E36]. This cash drain has forced the company to ramp up borrowings to Rs 174 Crore in March 2026, up sharply from Rs 73 Crore in the prior year [E39]. Furthermore, official filings carry an explicit warning flag noting that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E62]. Valuation risk is also evident in the Price-to-Book multiple of 5.93x against a sector benchmark of 2.42x, alongside high annualised volatility of 58.2% and a history of deep drawdowns reaching -48.8% [E7, E53, E54]. Conceded: the company exhibits strong trailing sales growth of 67% and a high return on equity of 32.0% [E17, E28].

Conceded: operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative Rs 64 Crore and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 79 Crore [E34, E35]. However, the bear's narrow focus on a single snapshot ignores the company's elite core profitability, evidenced by an outstanding ROE of 32.0% and an ROCE of 31.0%, both drastically outperforming sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13, E28]. While borrowings increased to Rs 174 Crore [E39], the enterprise trades at a very reasonable P/E of 15x to 16.01x, sitting below the sector benchmark of 22.54x and offering a stark discount to its calculated intrinsic value [E1, E6, E45]. The bear highlights high volatility and a historical drawdown [E53, E54], but overlooks the stellar 100 relative-strength rating and institutional money flow showing positive accumulation [E44, E51]. Furthermore, top-line and profit momentum are exceptionally strong, with compounded sales growth at 67% and profit growth at 295% in the trailing twelve months, supported by robust domestic and global demand for high and low voltage products [E17, E21, E77]. Finally, the rules-based screen awards the company a high-confidence 97 out of 100 score driven by massive year-over-year sales and net profit spikes [E63, E64, E66].

Conceded: the rules-based screen scores 97 out of 100 with strong reported sales and net profit growth [E63, E66]. However, the bull's focus on high ROE and ROCE of 32.0% and 31.0% [E12, E13] masks severe cash generation failures, as operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 64 Crore and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 79 Crore in March 2026 [E34, E35]. This divergence is underscored by a cash conversion ratio of -0.88x, where operating cash flow represents only -36% of operating profit [E33, E36]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes the balance sheet strain where borrowings more than doubled to Rs 174 Crore from Rs 73 Crore a year earlier [E39], alongside a flagged negative concerning potential capitalization of interest costs [E62]. While the bull leans on an attractive P/E multiple relative to the sector [E1, E6], the price-to-book ratio sits at an elevated 5.93x compared to the sector benchmark of 2.42x [E7]. Finally, the bull's reliance on momentum and relative strength [E44, E51] ignores high annualised volatility of 58.2% and an inconsistent quarterly operating margin trend over the last two quarters [E32, E54].

Conceded: operating cash flow was negative Rs 64 Crore and free cash flow was negative Rs 79 Crore in March 2026 [E34, E35]. However, the business operates in a sector experiencing a powerful tailwind with a score of +0.68, alongside sector median profit growth of 21.9% and sales growth of 18.6% [E68, E71, E72]. The bear's worry over elevated P/B ignores that the company trades at a reasonable P/E of 15x to 16.01x against a sector benchmark of 22.54x, offering a much more standard valuation lens [E1, E6]. Conceded: borrowings increased to Rs 174 Crore and the quarterly operating margin trend reads inconsistent over the last two quarters [E32, E39]. Yet, this is backed by an exceptional 31% ROCE and 32% ROE [E12, E13], alongside surging institutional money flow reflecting positive sentiment [E44]. Finally, the bear's fixation on volatility overlooks a rare relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, confirming that market strength is fully justified by top-tier operational expansion [E51, E64, E66].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 15x to 16.01x against a sector benchmark of 22.54x [E1, E6]. However, this valuation comfort is heavily undermined by an elevated price-to-book ratio of 5.85x to 5.93x, which stands starkly above the sector benchmark of 2.42x [E2, E7]. While the bull points to a tailwind score of +0.68 and robust growth metrics [E68, E71, E72], operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 64 Crore and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 79 Crore in March 2026, resulting in a troubling cash conversion of -0.88x [E33, E34, E35]. Conceded: institutional money flow reads positive [E44]. Yet, this capital influx sits atop a massive expansion in borrowings from Rs 73 Crore to Rs 174 Crore [E39], accompanied by explicit flags that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E62]. Finally, citing a relative-strength rating of 100 [E51] ignores that the stock carries an annualized volatility of 58.2% [E54], and the quarterly operating-margin trend is officially rated as inconsistent over the last two quarters [E32].
